question: The layer of earth that separates the crust from the core is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mantle.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The mantle: 

__
 
• The mantle extends up to a depth of 2900 km below the crust.
 
• It **separates the crust from the core**.
 
• The upper part of the mantle is known as the asthenosphere.
 
• Nearly 84% of the earth’s volume and 67% of the earth’s mass is occupied by the mantle.
 
• The major constituent elements of the mantle are Silicon and Magnesium and hence it is also termed as SIMA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**The crust:

 
• The crust is the uppermost layer over the earth’s surface.
 
• It is the thinnest layer.
 
• it is only about 5 km on the ocean floors, which mainly consists of silica and alumina thus called sial (si-silica and al-alumina), and 35 km on the continental masses, which mainly consists of silica and alumina.

The core:

 
• The innermost layer is the core with a radius of about 3500 km and divided into Inner and Outer core.
 
• It is called nife (ni – nickel and fe – ferrous – iron) as it's mainly made up of nickel and iron.
 
• Central core is called the Inner core and has a very high temperature and pressure.
